headlines.text: On a Saturday in 2025, back when the AEW World Heavyweight Title had a new owner by the end of the night as MJF vs. Adam Page vs. Samoa Joe vs. Swerve Strickland battled it out, appearing on Worlds End, rated 7.37 ? a solid showing ? ending the champion's reign at 2 defenses. It was the 70th time the AEW World Heavyweight Title had been on the line, a genuinely rare milestone for that title. MJF cashed in his Casino Gauntlet contract, capitalizing on a low blow to Adam Page to pin Samoa Joe and reclaim the AEW World Championship in a four-way also involving Swerve Strickland.

Flash back to 2023, when Eddie Kingston vs. Bryan Danielson met in a Continental Classic Semi-Final on Dynamite, rated 8.70 ? a match that lived up to every bit of hype, part of the special New Year's Smash '23 - Night 1 card.
Turning the clock back to 2024: Hook vs. Nick Wayne headlined Rampage, rated 6.12 in a hard-fought men's division clash ? part of that year's New Year's Smash '24.

secondaries.text: Flash back to 2025, when the AEW Continental Title changed hands as Jon Moxley vs. Kazuchika Okada battled it out, appearing on Worlds End, rated 6.98 ? ending the champion's reign at 13 defenses. In their first-ever meeting, Moxley defeated Kazuchika Okada in the Continental Classic final, ending Okada's 647-day reign and winning his first-ever C2 tournament.

Flash back to 2025, when Jon Moxley vs. Kyle Fletcher met in a Continental Classic Semi-Final on Worlds End, rated 9.36 ? an all-time classic ? part of a stacked Worlds End '25 card, rated 8.02 overall. Fletcher competed in the loaded Worlds End undercard as the Continental Classic and World Title storylines collided around him.

On this day in 2025, Babes Of Wrath vs. Athena & Mone put the AEW Women's World Tag Team Titles on the line, appearing on Worlds End, rated 6.67. For Athena & Mone, it marked a first real shot at championship gold.
